structure.heading: Threat Landscape and Verified Attack Paths (Q2 2026 Assessment Window)
text_content: **Threat Landscape and Verified Attack Paths (Q2 2026 Assessment Window)**

Between 2026-03-01 and 2026-04-15 the assessment recorded 18 high-severity threat events relevant to the enterprise. Incident categorization shows the top three observed tactics were phishing (8 events), credential stuffing (6 events), and exploitation of public-facing applications (4 events). Affected assets included externally facing Microsoft Exchange services, an external API gateway, and legacy remote desktop hosts. Industry telemetry associated several events with commodity cybercrime operators targeting account takeover and web-application CVEs. Event timelines indicate rapid escalation: mean time from initial foothold to detected lateral movement was under 48 hours in 10 of the 18 events, increasing the urgency for detection tuning.

Penetration testing completed on 2026-04-10 validated multiple verified attack paths and achieved domain administrator in 2 of 5 tested scenarios. Both successful scenarios exploited credential reuse and insufficient segmentation within Active Directory, enabling privilege escalation and persistent access to corporate file shares and domain services. In the three unsuccessful scenarios, controls such as enforced multi-factor authentication via Okta and segmented jump hosts disrupted full compromise. Time-to-compromise measurements showed lateral movement to domain controllers in under six hours for the two successful scenarios, highlighting gaps in host-level detection and privileged access logging.

Verified attack paths inform detection engineering and incident response without repeating remediation schedules. Key operational actions include: 1) tuning SIEM rules to detect lateral movement indicators seen in testing (Kerberos abuse, remote service creation); 2) expanding EDR to all domain-joined endpoints with kernel-level telemetry; 3) hardening public-facing applications with a WAF and automated scanning; and 4) executing a credential hygiene campaign targeting accounts involved in the 8 phishing and 6 credential-stuffing events. These measures will reduce dwell time and improve forensic fidelity for subsequent assessment windows and accelerate detection tuning.

Executive reporting will include the 2.6 score, trendline to the prior review, and target maturity increments tied to governance OKRs qaurterly.

2026 Cybersecurity Posture Assessment — Threat Alignment and Remediation Plan
Ref: CSA-26-0417 | Date: 22 February 2026 | Prepared for: Executive Risk Committee

Section Executive Summary
This assessment aligns the 2026 external threat landscape with verified penetration testing outcomes conducted between November 2025 and January 2026. Increased activity from ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) affiliates, credential-stuffing campaigns targeting SaaS platforms, and exploitation of edge device vulnerabilities materially affect the organisation’s risk profile. Testing confirmed that while perimeter controls have improved since Q2 2025, weaknesses in identity governance and legacy server patching continue to present exploitable pathways. The findings have been translated into a risk-prioritised 90-day remediation roadmap designed to reduce the enterprise’s aggregate risk exposure by an estimated 38%.

Section Threat Landscape 2026 Overview
Industry intelligence from FS-ISAC and ENISA highlights a 27% year-on-year rise in double-extortion ransomware and a marked increase in exploitation of zero-day vulnerabilities within network appliances. Adversaries are increasingly leveraging token replay and MFA fatigue attacks to bypass authentication safeguards. Our sector has experienced targeted phishing campaigns impersonating regulatory authorities, with payloads delivering remote access trojans via encrypted archives. These developments underscore the need for hardened identity controls and accelerated patch management for externally exposed systems.

Section Penetration Testing Outcomes
The independent red team identified 14 validated findings, including three critical and five high-severity vulnerabilities. A chained attack scenario demonstrated lateral movement from a compromised contractor VPN account to a Tier-2 application server due to excessive Active Directory group permissions. Web application testing uncovered a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability within the client reporting portal, though exploitation required authenticated access. Time-to-detect during the simulated ransomware deployment averaged 11 hours, exceeding the internal target of 4 hours and indicating gaps in endpoint telemetry correlation.

Section Control Maturity and Remediation Backlog
Control maturity was assessed using a 1–5 scale aligned to the NIST CSF. Identity and Access Management scored 2.6, Vulnerability Management 3.1, Security Monitoring 2.8, and Incident Response 3.4. The remediation backlog currently contains 186 open vulnerabilities, of which 42 are rated critical and have aged beyond the 30-day policy threshold. Resource constraints within infrastructure operations have delayed patch cycles for legacy Windows Server 2016 assets supporting finance applications.

Section Risk-Prioritised 90-Day Roadmap
The first 30 days will focus on enforcing phishing-resistant MFA for all privileged accounts and remediating the three critical findings validated during testing. By Day 60, the objective is to reduce critical vulnerability backlog by at least 70% through accelerated patch sprints and temporary network segmentation controls. Within 90 days, centralised log aggregation for all Tier-1 assets will be completed to reduce mean time to detect below 4 hours. Progress will be tracked against defined risk reduction metrics and reported monthly to the Executive Risk Committee.

sections.heading: 2026 Threat Landscape Alignment
sections.body: Threat intelligence collected between October 2025 and January 2026 indicates a 38% increase in credential-based attacks targeting cloud identity providers and a sustained rise in ransomware-as-a-service operations affecting mid-market enterprises. Adversaries are leveraging MFA fatigue techniques and exploiting unpatched edge devices to establish initial footholds. Sector-specific reporting from ISAC partners confirms active reconnaissance against our industry peers, particularly focused on third-party SaaS integrations. These trends materially elevate the likelihood of identity compromise and lateral movement within hybrid environments.

sections.heading: Penetration Testing Outcomes
sections.body: An independent penetration test conducted by RedVector Security in December 2025 identified 3 critical and 9 high-severity findings across external, internal, and cloud scopes. The most significant issue involved privilege escalation via misconfigured Azure AD conditional access policies, enabling simulated domain-wide access within 72 hours. External testing also revealed an exposed legacy VPN gateway vulnerable to CVE-2024-3178, which allowed authenticated remote code execution. While no evidence of active exploitation was found in production logs, the attack paths were reproducible and aligned with current threat actor tradecraft.

sections.heading: Control Maturity and Gap Analysis
sections.body: 7 SOC monitoring and recent EDR tuning improvements. However, asset management accuracy remains at 76%, constraining vulnerability prioritisation and increasing residual risk exposure.

sections.heading: Vulnerability Remediation Backlog
sections.body: As of 31 January 2026, the enterprise backlog includes 412 open vulnerabilities, of which 27 are critical and 103 are high severity. The median remediation time for critical findings is 41 days, exceeding the internal policy threshold of 15 days. Approximately 18% of critical exposures are tied to internet-facing systems, primarily legacy application servers pending modernization. Resource constraints within application teams and change window limitations are the primary contributors to backlog accumulation.

sections.heading: Risk-Prioritised 90-Day Roadmap
sections.body: The next 90 days will focus on eliminating internet-exposed critical vulnerabilities, enforcing phishing-resistant MFA for all privileged accounts, and decommissioning the legacy VPN gateway. A cross-functional remediation sprint has been established to reduce the critical backlog by 80% and high-severity backlog by 50% by the end of Q2 2026. Concurrently, automated asset discovery tooling will be expanded to achieve 95% coverage, directly improving risk visibility and patch prioritisation accuracy. Successful execution of this roadmap is projected to reduce modeled annualized loss expectancy by 29%.
